title: Sneakernet: bundle signing and verification playbook for air-gapped installs
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for preparing, signing, transporting, and validating offline bundles for air-gapped/private Redwood Inference installs. It focuses on a ‘sneakernet’ transfer pattern (physical media such as encrypted SSDs / AWS Snowball) and covers artifact manifest formats, signing options, Terraform notes for bundle-aware modules, verification steps on target clusters, and a conservative upgrade/rollback sequencing.

Status and scope:
- Draft: contains operational checklists and a minimal set of automation notes.
- Assumes the customer/partner provides an agreed C2 process for chain-of-custody.
- Does NOT replace the offline registry operator design doc; this is complementary and focuses on the human+operator workflows and lightweight automation for signing and verification.

High-level flow:
1) Curate artifacts (images, charts, operators, binaries, tf modules) and build a signed bundle directory.
2) Produce a machine-readable manifest with checksums and signatures.
3) Export bundle to physical media with encryption and tamper-evidence.
4) Transfer to customer site via agreed transport.
5) On target, validate checksums and signatures, seed local registry/registry-mirror, and run preflight smoke tests.
6) Perform upgrade according to sequencing with canary/parallel waves where possible.

Bundle layout (recommended):
- bundle-v{major}.{minor}.{patch}/
  - manifest.jsonl  -- newline-delimited records for each artifact (see manifest spec below)
  - catalogs/      -- helm/oci catalogs as tar/oci-layout directories
  - images/        -- docker tarballs (name_tag.tar), or OCI layout tarball per image
  - operators/     -- operator-bundles (csvs, manifests)
  - binaries/      -- cli binaries (sha256 in manifest)
  - tf-modules/    -- compressed module tarballs and README for install hooks
  - provenance/    -- signatures (cosign/gpg), attestations, and transfer log.txt

Manifest spec (simple, newline-delimited JSON entries):
- fields per entry: kind, name, version, path_relative, sha256, size_bytes, signing_scheme, signature_path
- Example entry: {"kind":"image","name":"redwood/runtime","version":"v1.3.2","path_relative":"images/redwood-runtime_v1.3.2.tar","sha256":"<hex>","size_bytes":"23421234","signing_scheme":"cosign","signature_path":"provenance/redwood-runtime_v1.3.2.sig"}
- Why newline-delimited? easier streaming/validation on constrained hosts, resilient to partial reads.

Signing options (recommendations and tradeoffs):
- cosign (recommended for images): supports OCI images, keyless (OIDC) or key-pair, and generates signatures and SBOM attestation. Use cosign for containers and any OCI-layout artifact.
- GPG (good for binaries/tf tarballs): well-understood and can be verified offline with public keys distributed in the bundle.
- Sigstore/fulcio/rekor is NOT available in air-gapped targets — prefer detached signatures and include public keys (or their fingerprints) inside provenance/.
- Include a bundle root signing manifest: a single signed file (bundle-root.json) that lists all manifest file hashes and bundle version. This file is signed using an organizational GPG key and an HSM-backed key where available.

Transport and media handling checklist:
- Prepare media (encrypted LUKS container on SSD, or vendor appliance like Snowball).
- Tooling: provide small verification tool on media (verify-bundle.sh) that validates root signature and manifest checksums before allowing copy.
- Labeling: tamper-evident seals + tamper log.txt appended at each handover step.
- Chain-of-custody: timestamped receipts with signer names and ID numbers (sample template included in provenance/transfer-receipts/).
- Recovery: keep a signed copy of bundle-root.json in cold storage (separate from media) in case of media failure.

On-target verification steps (operator checklist):
1) Mount media in isolated staging host (not yet connected to production network).
2) Run verify-bundle.sh which performs: root signature verification, manifest checksum validation, per-artifact sha256 checks.
3) If any signature check fails -> abort, capture error logs, and contact release owner.
4) Extract artifacts to local staging registry/mirror directories.
5) Seed registry: use registry-mirror tool to load tarballs or OCI-layout into the private registry. Document exact commands for registry product in use (Harbor/Quay/Kind-registry).
6) Run preflight smoke: deploy minimal control-plane pods (k8s manifests in bundle) with --dry-run and run health probes.
7) Approve upgrade window and proceed with rollout steps.

Upgrade sequencing (conservative plan):
- Pre-checks: verify resource quotas, run disk checks, backup etcd (if applicable), backup configmaps/secrets.
- Stage 0: dry-run of manifests against cluster (kubectl --server-dry-run).
- Stage 1: seed registry and operator images; run operator-only upgrade in isolated namespace.
- Stage 2: control-plane (if customer manages) upgrades for runtime components in waves (wave size = 10-25% of nodes depending on cluster size).
- Stage 3: data plane rollout (model servers, inference workers) with progressive traffic shifting and KPIs monitored (latency, error rate).
- Observability: ensure logs and metrics forwarding to local telemetry collector; if unavailable, run local smoke checks and store reports in provenance/upgrade-run-YYYYMMDD/.
- Rollback: always have an executable rollback plan per wave using previous bundle version and image tags. Do not delete old images until rollback window expires.

Terraform module notes (short):
- Modules should accept bundle_manifest and bundle_version as inputs. Example var: bundle_source = "file:///mnt/bundle-v1.2.3"
- Module responsibilities: configure registry credentials, create registry namespaces, deploy registry-seed Job (loads artifacts), and annotate deployed resources with bundle_version metadata.
- Provide a "confirm_seed" null_resource that depends on a verification script exit code so TF plan shows success/failure.
- Keep modules idempotent and tolerant of partial seeds (make seed job re-entrant by checking existing blobs by sha256).

Operational gotchas and hardened recommendations:
- Never trust timestamps from transfer logs alone; prefer signed receipts.
- Avoid mixing channel-level signing schemes; standardize (prefer cosign + GPG fallback).
- For very large bundles prefer layered transfer: critical control-plane artifacts first (~small subset) followed by data-plane images to reduce time to first-boot.
- Keep a minimal emergency bundle (control-plane-only) that can restore cluster control in minutes.

Open questions / decisions to finalize:
- Do we mandate HSM-backed root signing for all enterprise customers? pros: stronger key safety; cons: operational overhead for partners.
- Do we include Rekor-like append-only log snapshots in provenance/ for offline replays?
- What is the retention policy for signed bundles in customer & vendor archives (suggestion: 3 years for compliance customers).

Appendix: quick commands (examples)
- Generate cosign keypair: cosign generate-key-pair && cosign sign-blob --key cosign.key images/redwood-runtime_v1.3.2.tar
- Compute sha256: sha256sum images/redwood-runtime_v1.3.2.tar > images/redwood-runtime_v1.3.2.tar.sha256
- Verify manifest line: jq -c . manifest.jsonl | while read -r l; do echo $l | jq -r .path_relative | xargs -I{} sha256sum {} ; done
- Seed registry (example using skopeo/ctr/load): skopeo copy docker-archive:images/redwood-runtime_v1.3.2.tar dir:oci-layout-dir/ && ctr -n=k8s.io images import images/redwood-runtime_v1.3.2.tar

Notes to self (informal):

- Run tabletop with Solutions Eng to validate chain-of-custody steps next week.
- Sync with Terraform module owners on the confirm_seed hook behavior.

END OF PLAYBOOK
